page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.3xlarge is a compute-focused virtual machine instance within the High Clock Speed family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 12 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs based on an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. System memory totals 24.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance integrates a 10 Gbps baseline network interface to manage host and inter-service communications.

Hardware accelerators and direct-attached storage are not included with this instance profile. The server features 0 GPU devices and provisions 0 GB of local disk capacity, requiring workloads to rely on remote block storage for persistence. In addition, the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external IP or gateway assignment for public internet egress and ingress.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the allocation provides dense compute power at elevated base frequencies without the overhead cost of surplus RAM. This configuration avoids stranded memory capacity when supporting CPU-bound tasks. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local ephemeral NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O performance is bounded by remote network storage configurations.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.3xlarge is tailored for compute-heavy applications requiring dedicated thread execution and stable clock rates. Relevant deployments include software compilation, continuous integration runners, batch computing, media encoding, and compute-bound web tier services.
